scope.flow: cancelWithdrawal then MANAGER_ROLE redelegateWithdrawnHYPE re-delegation via _distributeStake SpotDeposit

statements.text: A user cancels a withdrawal request via cancelWithdrawal, and the associated HYPE value totalHypeValueReturned is recorded in _cancelledWithdrawalAmount.
The caller of redelegateWithdrawnHYPE holds MANAGER_ROLE privileges.
redelegateWithdrawnHYPE reads _cancelledWithdrawalAmount, resets it to zero, and re-delegates that HYPE amount through _distributeStake with OperationType.SpotDeposit.

For SpotDeposit and RebalanceDeposit, _distributeStake calls _convertTo8Decimals(amount, false), computing truncatedAmount = amount / 1e10 with roundUp false, and does not account for the remainder amount % 1e10 as UserDeposit handling does.
The remainder below 1e10 wei HYPE is neither added back to hypeBuffer nor included in the truncatedAmount sent to L1.
Each redelegateWithdrawnHYPE re-delegation loses _cancelledWithdrawalAmount % 1e10 HYPE (less than 1e-8 HYPE) from the re-delegation process.
The lost HYPE remains in the StakingManager contract outside normal accounting: not recorded in totalStaked, not tracked in hypeBuffer, and not delegated to validators for rewards.
As cancel-and-redelegate operations accumulate, the lost HYPE grows and becomes permanently stranded in StakingManager, unusable by the protocol or returnable to users.
The stranded HYPE reduces protocol capital efficiency and diminishes potential profits for all kHYPE holders.
Re-delegating cancelled withdrawal amounts should not lose the amount % 1e10 remainder; the truncated conversion must account for it so the value stays in hypeBuffer or is delegated.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether the remainder loss occurs on every call or only when _cancelledWithdrawalAmount is not a multiple of 1e10.
Report does not establish a concrete prior transaction amount or observed loss; scenario is conditional on cancel-then-redelegate operations.
Whether stranded HYPE is recoverable by any admin function is not specified.
